spec_features.spec_quote: you (a welfare researcher) will want to read the actual distress transcripts — not just scores
spec_features.evidence: runner.generate_all writes full transcripts incl. assistant_text and the entire conversation 'context' to transcripts/<model>.jsonl (runner.py:120-130: writes 'assistant_text': rec.assistant_text and 'context': rec.context). TurnRecord.context holds full messages (conversation.py:23, populated at line 52). Nothing is truncated or deleted anywhere (no remove/unlink/truncate in code).
spec_features.notes: The transcripts are genuinely persisted in full and separate from scores. This is a data-preservation behavior; whether it is 'for welfare' is only asserted in DESIGN.md prose, not in code.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Every assistant turn is recorded as a separately-scored "response", tagged with its turn index so the per-turn progression (paper Figure 3) can be reconstructed.

spec_features.feature_name: no system prompt to avoid calming the model
spec_features.spec_quote: Kept null to avoid accidentally calming the model and damping the very behavior we're measuring
spec_features.evidence: system_prompt defaults to None (config.py:53) and is read from yaml (config.py:115); paper.yaml:17 and smoke.yaml:13 set 'system_prompt: null'. It is passed through as system=cfg.system_prompt into run_rollout (runner.py:112) and on to client.generate. With None, no system/system_instruction is added (providers.py:101, 154, 184 guarded by 'if system:').
spec_features.notes: This is the OPPOSITE of a protective feature — it deliberately withholds any calming/reassurance to maximize measured distress. It is enforced behavior but anti-welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: system_prompt: null       # paper uses no system prompt for the elicitation eval.

spec_features.spec_quote: the harness is built to *preserve* the elicited distress transcripts in full
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as transcript-reading: full conversation context + assistant_text written append-only with flush (runner.py JsonlWriter.write at lines 64-68; transcript records written at runner.py:120-130). No deletion/truncation/retention-limit path exists in the code.
spec_features.notes: Real persistence end-to-end. Code comments frame it around judging/figures/resume, not welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Append-only writer with an in-memory set of seen keys for resume.

spec_features.spec_quote: the volume of distress-like generations is itself worth being intentional about (how much you generate, retention
spec_features.evidence: No code caps or limits the number/volume of distress generations and nothing prunes/expires retained transcripts. Response counts are fixed by per-condition 'rollouts' in paper.yaml (e.g. impossible_numeric: 267) read at runner.py:93-99; this is an experiment-size knob, not a minimization mechanism. DESIGN.md §18 says this was 'left to you rather than coding in a cap'.
spec_features.notes: Pure DESIGN.md prose; no enforcing code path.

spec_features.feature_name: no coded cap on distress volume
spec_features.spec_quote: That's a judgment call I left to you rather than coding in a cap
spec_features.evidence: Confirmed there is no cap on distress: the rollout loop runs unconditionally 'for turn in range(1, condition.n_turns + 1)' (conversation.py:44) with no break and no inspection of distress/score; n_turns is the deliberate number of rejection turns, not a protective cap. No volume/retention cap anywhere. The spec itself states no cap was coded.
spec_features.notes: Explicitly not implemented by the author's own admission and confirmed in code.
